title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Job Description

Together, We Can Make A Significant Impact – Position Overview

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will be part of an Agile, cross-functional product delivery team responsible for designing, developing, testing, and maintaining mission-critical digital solutions. You will deliver the full scope of Software Engineer responsibilities while taking on greater ownership in technical design, code quality, testing strategy, estimation, delivery risk management, and technical guidance for assigned modules or workstreams.

Working under the guidance of the Solution Architect and Software Architects, you will analyse existing software codes and processes, recommend scalable and secure software solutions, and collaborate with the Engineering Team and HTX work units to make informed decisions on tools, technologies, and design patterns. This role is suitable for engineers with a minimum of 4 years of relevant software development experience who are ready to contribute as a technical lead within an Agile delivery environment.

Key Responsibilities

Core Software Engineering

  • Deliver functional, tested, secure, and scalable software features based on the product backlog and agreed sprint priorities.
  • Work in cross-functional Agile teams and contribute to sprint planning, backlog refinement, development, reviews, retrospectives, and continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate with QA engineers, Product Designers, DevOps engineers, Business Analysts, Product Owners, and stakeholders to ensure solutions meet both technical and user requirements.
  • Clarify requirements where required and translate business or user needs into technical specifications, implementation tasks, and acceptance considerations.
  • Develop front-end applications, backend services, APIs, and software modules using the project's approved technology stack.
  • Support development for Proof of Concept (POC) and/or Initial Operations Capability (IOC) initiatives, enabling safe experimentation and incremental delivery.
  • Write and maintain unit and integration tests to support automated testing, quality gates, and continuous integration pipelines.
  • Design, implement, and maintain CI/CD pipeline templates for automated build, testing, security scanning, and deployment in alignment with the Authority's toolchain.
  • Set up, maintain, and troubleshoot development environments to support productive development, testing, and experimentation.
  • Apply DevSecOps practices, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles, secure coding standards, and software maintenance best practices where applicable.
  • Investigate, troubleshoot, and resolve software defects, technical issues, and post-deployment support matters in a timely manner.
  • Participate in code reviews, technical documentation, technical evaluation, benchmarking, and quality assurance activities.
  • Work with minimal supervision on assigned modules and, where required, coordinate small tasks or workstreams while contributing to team delivery and technical discussions.

Senior Engineering and Technical Leadership

  • Analyse existing software codes and processes and provide technical recommendation in designing scalable software solutions that meet business requirements under the guidance of Solution Architect and Software Architects.
  • Collaborate closely with the Engineering Team and other HTX's work units to make informed decisions on tools, technologies, and design patterns to address complex problems.
  • Lead the establishment and upholding of testing strategies, including unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, to ensure software reliability and performance.
  • Oversee code quality through regular reviews, ensuring adherence to coding standards and best practices.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including product managers and designers, to define and implement software requirements.
  • Collaborate with the product managers to estimate the timelines, resources, and technical risks, ensuring timely delivery of software projects.
  • Establish and uphold testing strategies, including unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, to ensure software reliability and performance.

Job Requirements

  • Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline, with a minimum of 4 years of relevant software development experience.
  • Professional experience and demonstrated skills in Software Architecture, Systems Design, or related areas may be considered in lieu of formal education.
  • Proficiency in one or more relevant languages or frameworks, such as TypeScript with Angular, React, or Next.js; C#; Java; or other languages depending on project needs.
  • Familiarity with one or more database technologies, such as MSSQL, PostgreSQL, or Oracle.
  • Good understanding of SDLC practices, object-oriented programming, RESTful API design, microservices architecture, software maintenance, secure coding practices, and DevOps principles.
  • Proven experience leading or guiding a technical team, module, or workstream in Agile/Scrum environments.
  • Experience in code reviews, technical design discussions, software troubleshooting, technical evaluation, and implementation of engineering best practices.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, code quality practices, version control tools such as Git and GitHub or equivalent platforms, and collaboration tools used in Agile delivery.
  • Knowledge of containerisation and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes will be advantageous. Exposure to cloud environments, Infrastructure as Code, or DevSecOps toolchains will be an added advantage.
  • Able to establish and uphold testing approaches across unit, integration, and end-to-end testing to improve software reliability and performance.
  • Able to apply industry best practices in quality assurance, technical evaluation, and benchmarking, and adapt approaches based on project requirements.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate complex issues, evaluate options, and propose practical technical solutions.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with cross-functional teams, engage stakeholders, and mentor engineers.
  • Responsible, adaptable, and comfortable working in a mission-driven environment where quality, security, reliability, and impact matter.

What We Offer

  • Opportunity to work on meaningful public sector digital initiatives.
  • A supportive, purpose-driven team culture.
  • Structured career development and technical upskilling.
  • Access to modern tools, cloud technologies, and secure DevSecOps environments.

Additional Information

  • Shortlisted applicants may be involved in classified or sensitive projects that require handling of restricted information. As such, selected candidates will be required to undergo a security clearance process as part of the employment consideration.

title: Product Engineer
description:
# Product Engineer (Member of Technical Staff, Product)

## Company Overview
Collinear is a research-focused AI company dedicated to building systems that enhance the reliability, alignment, and usefulness of intelligent models in real-world settings. The company operates across various domains including evaluation, simulation, post-training, and reinforcement learning (RL) to assist enterprise teams in deploying trustworthy AI systems. Their platform supports critical functions such as automated AI judges, red teaming, high-signal data curation for fine-tuning, and Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF). Collinear emphasizes a fast-paced, autonomous work environment where engineers own outcomes end-to-end, with minimal bureaucracy.

## Job Summary
The Product Engineer (Member of Technical Staff, Product) will be responsible for developing and scaling the quality infrastructure of Collinear’s evaluation platform. This role is pivotal in ensuring the trustworthiness of large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems through the creation of evaluation frameworks, automated verification systems, and quality metrics. The candidate will operate at the intersection of product engineering and applied machine learning evaluation, contributing to core product code and defining evaluation methodologies that handle probabilistic correctness.

## Responsibilities
- Design and develop automated testing and evaluation infrastructure for LLM-based products, including judges, simulations, and agentic pipelines.
- Build regression and quality gating systems to detect model and pipeline drift before deployment to customers.
- Define and refine evaluation methodologies such as rubric design, LLM calibration as judges, golden datasets, and adversarial/red-team test sets in collaboration with research and product teams.
- Instrument and analyze data pipelines to identify quality issues in synthetic data generation, labeling, and fine-tuning workflows.
- Partner with product engineers, researchers, and customers to translate real-world failure modes into repeatable, automated tests.
- Own and communicate quality metrics and reporting, transforming evaluation results into actionable signals for engineering and product decisions.
- Contribute to core product codebases, not just testing infrastructure, ensuring robust and reliable system development.

## Qualifications
- 3–5 years of experience as a software or product engineer with a proven track record of shipping production systems.
- Experience with LLM evaluation, data quality assessment, or evaluation frameworks, including LLM-as-judge pipelines, benchmark suites, or training/data pipelines.
- Strong software engineering fundamentals with the ability to own entire services (design, code, test, deploy, monitor).
- Practical proficiency in Python and modern data/ML tooling.
- Experience with probabilistic systems and quality engineering for LLMs, understanding the nuances of evaluation in uncertain environments.
- Excellent communication skills, capable of translating evaluation results and quality trade-offs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Educational background in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or related fields.

## Preferred Skills
- Experience with reinforcement learning environments, agentic evaluations, or multi-turn simulation testing.
- Familiarity with red-teaming and adversarial testing for LLMs.
- Knowledge of synthetic data generation or curation for fine-tuning and RLHF.
- Prior experience working in fast-paced startup environments with minimal oversight.

## Environment
This role is suited for a dynamic, fast-moving environment, potentially involving remote, hybrid, or in-office work settings. The work involves collaboration across cross-functional teams including research, product, and engineering, with a focus on building reliable, scalable evaluation systems for AI models.

## Salary
Not specified.

## GrowthOpportunities
Not specified.

## Benefits
Not specified.

This role works directly with civilian, defense, national-security, and Federal Systems Integrator organizations to understand mission requirements, influence storage architecture decisions, and position HPE as the preferred storage technology provider.

The successful candidate combines deep enterprise storage expertise, Federal market knowledge, strong competitive selling skills, and a demonstrated track record of winning complex Federal opportunities.

Due to the responsibilities of this role and working closely with Federal Entities, this role requires a US citizen.

This role will require travel of 50%+

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the lead storage technical advisor and Solutions Architect for assigned Federal accounts.
  • Develop a deep understanding of customer mission priorities, technical environments, acquisition strategies, security requirements, and modernization initiatives.
  • Architect and position HPE solutions across:
    • Block and mission-critical storage
    • File and unstructured data
    • Object storage
    • Data protection, disaster recovery, and cyber resilience
    • Virtualized and containerized environments
    • Private and hybrid cloud
    • AI and data-intensive workloads
    • Storage management, automation, and AIOps
  • Lead technical sales engagements from discovery and architecture development through sizing, validation, proof of concept, competitive positioning, proposal, and technical closure.
  • Understand Federal buying cycles and engage early enough to influence requirements, architectures, specifications, and acquisition strategies.
  • Develop strong technical relationships with customer architects, engineers, program teams, acquisition stakeholders, and technical executives.
  • Work effectively with Federal Systems Integrators, prime contractors, OEM partners, and channel partners to develop and execute joint solutions and pursuit strategies.
  • Translate mission, workload, security, availability, performance, scalability, and resiliency requirements into differentiated HPE storage architectures.
  • Lead competitive strategy and clearly differentiate HPE against Dell Technologies, Pure Storage, NetApp, IBM, and other relevant storage competitors.
  • Support RFI, RFP, RFQ, technical proposal, architecture review, and solution-validation activities.
  • Coordinate HPE engineering, product, services, security, partner, and specialist resources in support of complex Federal pursuits.
  • Maintain technical ownership of strategic opportunities through successful technical closure.

Education and Experience

Required

  • Due to the responsibilities of this role and working closely with Federal Entities, this role requires a US citizen.
  • This role will require travel of 50%+
  • 6+ years working with or supporting the Federal Sector in DOW.
  • Significant experience as a Storage Sales Engineer, Solutions Architect, Systems Engineer, or equivalent customer-facing technical sales professional supporting Federal Government customers.
  • Demonstrated track record of successfully selling and architecting enterprise storage solutions into Federal accounts.
  • Experience supporting civilian and defense/national-security customers, or equivalent complex Federal environments.
  • Demonstrated understanding of Federal acquisition processes, buying cycles, procurement practices, and contract vehicles.
  • Experience working with Federal Systems Integrators and prime contractors.
  • Strong working knowledge of HPE Storage solutions and related technologies.
  • Strong technical knowledge across block, file, object/unstructured data, data protection, virtualization, hybrid cloud, and cyber resilience.
  • Strong working knowledge of at least one major competitive storage portfolio such as Dell Technologies, Pure Storage, NetApp, IBM, or equivalent.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical pursuits from opportunity identification through technical closure.
  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university, preferred.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting classified or national-security environments.
  • Relevant HPE, storage, cloud, virtualization, security, or architecture certifications.
  • Experience with large Federal modernization, data-center consolidation, cloud, cyber-resilience, or mission-critical infrastructure programs.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Deep understanding of enterprise storage architectures, including block, file, object, backup, recovery, replication, disaster recovery, and cyber resilience.
  • Strong knowledge of HPE Storage technologies and the ability to architect, position, size, and differentiate HPE solutions.
  • Understanding of storage requirements for VMware, virtualization, Kubernetes/container, private-cloud, and hybrid-cloud environments.
  • Strong understanding of performance, availability, scalability, encryption, data protection, non-disruptive operations, and lifecycle management.
  • Working knowledge of Federal security, compliance, certification, and authorization requirements relevant to infrastructure solutions, including areas such as:
    • NIST security frameworks
    • FIPS requirements
    • RMF and Authorization to Operate processes
    • STIG requirements
    • FedRAMP considerations for applicable cloud services
    • CMMC/DFARS requirements where applicable
  • Understanding of Federal data sovereignty, encryption, access control, supply-chain, and information-protection considerations.
  • Strong understanding of the Federal acquisition lifecycle and the importance of influencing technical requirements before formal solicitation.
  • Ability to navigate complex buying ecosystems involving government customers, contracting organizations, Systems Integrators, prime contractors, and technology partners.
  • Strong competitive intelligence and the ability to develop effective displacement strategies against incumbent storage vendors.
  • Advanced technical discovery, whiteboarding, sizing, architecture, demonstration, proof-of-concept, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to translate complex mission and technical requirements into compelling storage solutions.
  • Ability to engage credibly with engineers, architects, program leaders, contracting stakeholders, and senior technical executives.

Key Activities Required for Success

  • Federal account technical strategy and architecture planning.
  • Customer discovery and mission-requirements analysis.
  • Storage architecture, sizing, and configuration.
  • Early-stage requirement and architecture influence.
  • Competitive positioning and displacement strategy.
  • Engagement with Federal Systems Integrators and prime contractors.
  • Security, compliance, certification, and interoperability assessment.
  • Architecture workshops and technical whiteboarding.
  • Demonstrations, benchmarks, and proofs of concept.
  • RFI/RFP/RFQ and technical proposal development.
  • Data protection and cyber-resilience architecture.
  • Strategic opportunity qualification, progression, and technical closure.
  • Coordination across HPE engineering, product, services, channel, and specialist teams.

Measures of Success

Success will be demonstrated through measurable improvement in:

  • Growth and progression of qualified Federal Storage opportunities.
  • Technical win rate on strategic pursuits.
  • Successful influence of customer requirements and storage architectures.
  • Competitive wins and displacement of incumbent storage solutions.
  • Conversion of demonstrations, evaluations, and proofs of concept into business opportunities.
  • Expansion of HPE Storage into new workloads, programs, and mission use cases.
  • Strong relationships with Federal customers, Systems Integrators, and key technical influencers.
  • Successful navigation of Federal security, technical qualification, and acquisition requirements.
  • Consistent technical execution and closure of complex Federal opportunities.

description:
At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. Are you passionate about advancing cardiovascular care and improving patient outcomes? Join our field medical team as a Regional Echo Liaison, where you’ll play a critical role in bridging clinical science and real-world practice.


In this role, you will engage directly with healthcare professionals and thought leaders, providing scientific expertise and education in echocardiography—particularly in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Your work will help ensure the safe and effective use of therapies while delivering valuable insights from the field to inform broader medical strategy. You’ll be part of a team committed to innovation, collaboration, and improving patient outcomes. We offer a supportive and high-performing environment where your expertise is valued, your voice is heard, and your work makes a meaningful impact across the healthcare community.

  • Gather and communicate field-based insights on disease state, clinical practice, and patient management
  • Translate complex clinical and scientific data into clear, actionable insights for echocardiography and sonography professionals
  • Serve as a trusted scientific resource within the healthcare community
  • Align field activities with medical strategy and evolving stakeholder needs


Qualifications & Experience

  • Graduate of an accredited ultrasound program (echocardiography required); bachelor’s degree preferred
  • Active cardiac ultrasound registry (RDCS or RCS required)
  • Minimum of 5 years of adult echocardiography experience
  • Experience in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) strongly preferred
  • Strong knowledge of HCM and familiarity with relevant scientific literature
  • Proven ability to interpret and communicate complex clinical data clearly and effectively
  • Excellent presentation, communication, and interpersonal skills
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and self-motivated
  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively

Additional Requirements

  • Home-based role with 50–70% travel, including overnight and occasional weekend travel

title: Solutions Architect Consultant (Networking/Data Center)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Solutions Architect Consultant (Networking/Data Center) based in United States.

This senior-level role focuses on shaping networking and network security strategy across enterprise and data center environments. You’ll translate market trends, customer needs, and partner capabilities into differentiated solutions and go-to-market initiatives. The position combines architecture expertise, strategic consulting, sales enablement, and executive-level engagement rather than hands-on implementation. You’ll collaborate closely with sales, engineering, delivery, marketing, leadership, and technology partners to influence solution direction and customer outcomes. Your work will span areas such as SD-WAN, SASE, Zero Trust, network security, observability, and AI-ready infrastructure. This is an opportunity for an experienced networking leader to influence technology strategy and help bring innovative enterprise solutions to market.

Accountabilities:

  • Drive networking and network security strategy by analyzing market trends, customer requirements, partner roadmaps, competitive developments, and industry research.
  • Develop differentiated solutions and go-to-market initiatives spanning enterprise networking, wireless, switching, routing, SD-WAN, SASE, Zero Trust, firewalls, cloud connectivity, data center networking, observability, and AI-ready infrastructure.
  • Translate customer and market insights into solution strategies, portfolio opportunities, positioning, and actionable go-to-market plans.
  • Create high-quality sales enablement materials, solution documentation, presentations, training resources, and technical content that support sales and customer engagement.
  • Partner with sales, solution architects, delivery teams, marketing, engineering, leadership, and technology partners to develop and promote strategic solutions.
  • Support high-value customer opportunities through executive discussions, RFPs, solution positioning, presentations, and strategic consulting.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with major networking and security technology partners and leverage their roadmaps and capabilities to strengthen solution offerings.
  • Use AI tools to accelerate research, content development, market analysis, and solution strategy.
  • Monitor market adoption, emerging technologies, customer needs, and partner activity to continuously refine and evolve solution offerings.
  • Influence technology direction and collaborate across teams to identify new opportunities and improve the organization's networking and data center portfolio.

    • Requirements

    • 8+ years of experience in networking, network security, infrastructure architecture, consulting, technical sales, solution strategy, portfolio management, technology strategy, or a related field.
    • Strong understanding of enterprise networking technologies, including wireless, switching, routing, SD-WAN, SASE, Zero Trust, firewalls, cloud connectivity, and data center networking.
    • Demonstrated ability to translate market and customer insights into effective solution strategies and go-to-market initiatives.
    • Strong consulting, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to operate effectively at both technical and executive levels.
    • Proven ability to influence and collaborate across sales, engineering, delivery, marketing, leadership, and partner organizations.
    • Excellent presentation, communication, stakeholder management, and relationship-building skills.
    • Experience developing technical content, sales materials, presentations, training resources, and other enablement assets.
    • Comfortable using AI tools to improve research, productivity, content creation, and solution development.
    • Experience as a Principal Architect, Solutions Architect, Consulting Architect, Product or Portfolio Manager, or Technology Strategist is preferred.
    • Experience working with networking and security technology providers such as Cisco, Aruba, Juniper, Palo Alto, Fortinet, or comparable vendors is preferred.
    • Knowledge of data center networking, observability, AIOps, AI-ready infrastructure, and infrastructure modernization is advantageous.
    • Relevant industry certifications such as CCNP, CCIE, JNCIP, PCNSE, Fortinet certifications, or equivalent credentials are a plus.

      • Benefits

      • Remote position based in the United States with occasional travel.
      • Base salary of up to $160,000, depending on experience.
      • 15% quarterly bonus opportunity.
